properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 4 at 1:49PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Goldstream Valley and Nenana Hills-Lower Koyukuk Valley-Central
Interior-Dalton Highway Summits-Eielson AFB and Salcha-Two
Rivers-Upper Chena River Valley-White Mountains and High Terrain
South of the Yukon River-Upper Koyukuk Valley-Middle Yukon
Valley-Nenana-Chatanika River Valley-Fairbanks Metro Area

24 Hour rainfall totals across portions of the Western and Central
Interior have generally been between 0.75 and 1.25 inches due to
widespread moderate rainfall. This is a direct result of an
atmospheric river which continues to focus higher than normal levels
of moisture across the region.

Additional rainfall of .50 to as much as 1.50" inches will be
possible Friday evening through Saturday afternoon as a disturbance
aloft moves through and further interacts with the available
atmospheric moisture. Should this occur, 48 hours rainfall will
coincide with 5 to 10 year return intervals with locations receiving
the heaviest rainfall closer to 25 year return intervals.

While main stem rivers will be able to handle this extra volume of
water, some of the smaller feeder streams and rivers could see near
bankfull to minor flooding conditions. In addition increased stream
flows are expected for the next few days, so anyone planning
recreation activities on or along these waterways should exercise
extreme caution and be on the lookout for rapidly rising water
levels.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 5 to 8 feet with local sets to 10 feet and dangerous
and potentially life threatening rip currents, largest on
south- facing shores.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Saturday to 11 PM PDT Tuesday, peaking Sunday
and Monday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents will be widespread and very strong, potentially
pulling swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves
can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and
capsize small boats near shore. Enhanced beach erosion will
occur. Flooding of sea water is likely, around the time of
high tide, over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas such as
parking lots, beaches, and walkways. Areas most susceptible to
coastal flooding will include Avalon, Long Beach (Alamitos
Peninsula), and Oxnard to Malibu (including Point Mugu).

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides at 6.3 feet will occur around
5pm on Saturday, 6.7 feet at 6pm on Sunday, 7 feet at 7pm on
Monday, and 7.2 feet at 8pm on Tuesday.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks. Follow advice from local
officials. Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

after midnight tonight and continue falling to 11.1 feet
Wednesday morning.

feet on 03/12/2016.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

deaths occur in vehicles.

through flooded areas.

peak at 1 foot or less above the normal highest tide line, similar
to observed water levels on Thursday morning. At these levels, no

Kwigillingok, Kongiganak, and Quinhagak. High tide water levels
are then expected to fall as we continue through Sunday and
Monday.

The Shelby County Health Department has issued a Code Orange Ozone
Forecast effective for Shelby County Tennessee, Crittenden County
Arkansas, and DeSoto County Mississippi, including the city of
Memphis for today. This ozone forecast is due to forecasted ozone
values that will be unhealthy for sensitive groups. These values will
exceed the Environmental Protection Agency's federal safe health
standard. The Shelby County Health Department recommends that
sensitive groups which include active children and adults, and
people with respiratory disease, such as asthma, limit prolonged
outdoor exertion.

Please continue to check the latest air quality forecasts and updates
until monitored values return to safe levels. For more information go
to www.airnow.gov.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 3 at 11:18AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Central Interior-Nenana-Two Rivers-Middle Yukon Valley-Upper Koyukuk
Valley-Upper Chena River Valley-Fairbanks Metro Area-Goldstream
Valley and Nenana Hills-Lower Koyukuk Valley-Dalton Highway
Summits-Chatanika River Valley-White Mountains and High Terrain South
of the Yukon River-Eielson AFB and Salcha

Areas of 1 to 2.5 inches of rainfall are expected over the next 48
hours due to an atmospheric river. Average return intervals of 2 to 5
years is possible throughout much of the central and western interior
through the weekend. Isolated areas could potentially see heavy
rainfall more in line with 10 to even 25 year return intervals,
resulting in significant rises in the smaller headwater streams that
feed the Koyukuk and Middle Yukon Rivers. While there are no
immediate concerns for the main stem rivers in the area, they will
also see significant rises in water levels through the week as a
result of the expected heavy rainfall with sandbars potentially
becoming covered with water.

Across the Chena River basin, moderate to heavy rainfall of up to 1.5
inches is expected. This will also result in rises along the Chena
and Little Chena rivers. At this time flooding is not expected, but
should the focus for heaviest rainfall shift further east with time,
this could change.

Rainfall rates are expected to decrease by Sunday afternoon across
most of the area.
